method: isolated sub-agent; source review and fresh browser context

target.pageType: Read: component icon catalogue and usage documentation

scope.scoreBasis: current source, page rendering, and browser interaction evidence only

designSpecificity.verdict: Moderate to strong; content and interaction are tailored to the LinkX icon library, while the visual frame remains the standard VitePress documentation shell.
evidence: Chinese meaning and English key are co-located with each icon preview.
Categories distinguish sidebar, interaction, feedback, priority, business, supplemental, and compatibility names.
English key and Chinese usage terms filter the same catalogue.
Cards copy the LxIcon usage snippet rather than only exposing an abstract icon asset.

heuristics.name: Visibility of System Status
heuristics.reason: Copy success/failure and no-results are confirmed; successful result counts are visible in group labels but absent from the live status region.

heuristics.name: Match Between System and Real World
heuristics.reason: Chinese use meanings, English icon keys, recognizable previews, and domain categories match the library lookup task.

heuristics.name: User Control and Freedom
heuristics.reason: Users can clear search, reopen or collapse groups, and recover focus after clearing; copy has no undo but is a predictable action.

heuristics.name: Consistency and Standards
heuristics.reason: Cards, group disclosures, counts, theme, and native details keyboard behavior are consistent.

heuristics.name: Error Prevention
heuristics.reason: Visible icon meaning and key reduce wrong choices, though the initially open group presents 13 adjacent choices.

heuristics.name: Recognition Rather Than Recall
heuristics.reason: Each card shows icon, Chinese meaning, and English key; the search placeholder provides bilingual examples.

heuristics.name: Flexibility and Efficiency of Use
heuristics.reason: Search, grouped browsing, and keyboard navigation provide useful alternate paths; there is no direct search-focus shortcut or favorites.

heuristics.name: Aesthetic and Minimalist Design
heuristics.reason: The catalogue is orderly and task-focused, with some viewport competition from the standard docs navigation shell.

heuristics.name: Help Users Recognize, Diagnose, and Recover from Errors
heuristics.reason: Clipboard failure uses plain language and focuses a selected manual-copy snippet.

heuristics.name: Help and Documentation
heuristics.reason: The page documents size, motion, use, checklist coverage, addition rules, and compatibility aliases.

failedItems.name: Chunking
failedItems.evidence: Several groups exceed four items; P1 has 26 and P2 has 29 cards.

failedItems.name: Minimal choices
failedItems.evidence: P0 opens by default with 13 cards; opening P1/P2 exposes 26/29 cards.

mitigations: Search for undo yielded one visible result; Chinese 登出 yielded one visible result.

emotionalJourney: The title and bilingual hint make the entry point legible; filtered results reduce the catalogue; copy success confirms the resulting snippet. Clipboard denial has an actionable selected-code fallback. The empty message identifies the state but does not suggest recovery.
strengths: Bilingual search and category grouping narrow a 96-name catalogue effectively.
Copy failure recovery focuses and selects a usable code snippet.
Desktop themes and narrow layouts remain legible without document-level horizontal overflow.

priorityIssues.title: Non-empty search results are not announced in the live status region
priorityIssues.evidence: Browser search `undo` produced one visible card and group label `P0 高频核心（1）`, while `search-status` text remained empty. The source renders status text only for the no-results case.
priorityIssues.userImpact: Screen-reader users do not get an immediate spoken result count after typing and may need to continue tabbing to discover whether a match exists.
priorityIssues.recommendation: Announce the count for non-empty results in the existing polite live region; preserve the current no-results message.

priorityIssues.title: Category browsing exposes long card grids
priorityIssues.evidence: P0 is expanded initially with 13 cards; P1 and P2 contain 26 and 29 cards when opened.
priorityIssues.userImpact: Users browsing by meaning must scan many adjacent options at one decision point; search reduces the load when the key or synonym is known.
priorityIssues.recommendation: Consider smaller semantic subgroups or a shorter default expanded set while retaining search as a direct path.

priorityIssues.title: The 320px search placeholder truncates its final example
priorityIssues.evidence: The 320px screenshot displays the beginning of the bilingual example but clips the trailing `登出` example.
priorityIssues.userImpact: The search still works, but the hint is incomplete on the narrowest tested viewport.
priorityIssues.recommendation: Use a shorter placeholder at narrow widths and move examples into a concise wrapping hint.

redFlags: Semantic browsing can require scanning 13-29 cards; typing a known key reduces this to a single result.
No keyboard blocker was found in the tested clear, disclosure, and copy flow.
A non-empty result count is not announced through the polite live region.
passedEvidence: Tab reached the clear button; Enter cleared search and returned focus to the input.
Space opened a native details summary; Tab reached a named icon button with a 2px focus outline; Enter copied it.
Clipboard failure text is in a status region and the fallback code field is focused and selected.

redFlags: At 320px the last search example is clipped in the placeholder.
passedEvidence: The 375px and 320px document scroll widths equal their viewport widths.
The alias table scrolls inside its labelled region and displays a narrow-screen hint.
Mobile clear target is 44x44px and icon cards are approximately 96px high.

minorObservations: The empty result is clearly visible and the search clear button remains available, but the message does not mention that recovery path.
Reduced motion disables the loading icon animation (animation-name none, duration 0s); tile transition duration computes to 0.00001s.
boundaries: Assessment A only; Assessment B, detector/overlay reports, and code-review results were not viewed.
Clipboard branches used deterministic page-context stubs; the real desktop clipboard was not changed or verified.
NVDA/VoiceOver, physical touchscreen hardware, and 200% zoom were not tested.
Findings and scores describe the final page state observed on 2026-10-06.
